title: Glossary of Automotive Brake Terms
intro: Short, beginner-friendly definitions of the terms used in this guide. Use the search box or letter buttons to jump to a term.
objectives: Understand and use accurate brake system terminology.
Look up unfamiliar words quickly while studying other chapters.
summary: Accurate terminology prevents mistakes when reading service information and communicating findings.

items.d: A system that prevents wheel lock-up during hard braking by rapidly adjusting brake pressure at individual wheels.
A mechanism, usually in drum brakes, that keeps shoe-to-drum clearance correct as lining wears.
Trapped air that compresses under pressure, causing a soft or spongy pedal.
A small spring or clip that holds a pad firmly in position to reduce noise.
The fixed plate in a drum brake that holds the shoes, wheel cylinder and hardware.
A gentle break-in procedure that lets new friction material and rotors or drums wear to match each other.
A small valve on a caliper or wheel cylinder that is opened to release air and fluid.
The process of removing air and old fluid from the brake hydraulic system.
A device that multiplies pedal force to reduce driver effort.
A temporary loss of braking effectiveness caused by overheating.
The special hydraulic fluid that transmits pressure through the brake system.
A flexible, reinforced line that carries brake fluid to a part that moves, such as a caliper.
A rigid steel tube that carries brake fluid along the vehicle.
A friction part with a steel backing plate that presses against a disc rotor.
A curved friction part that presses outward against the inside of a brake drum.
The distance a vehicle travels after the brakes are applied until it stops.
The force that opposes the vehicle's motion when the brakes are applied.
The housing that holds the pads and piston(s) of a disc brake.
The hydraulic piston that pushes the brake pad toward the rotor.
A wedge placed against a wheel to prevent the vehicle from rolling.
Fluid, grease or oil on friction surfaces that reduces braking.
A measuring instrument used to measure small movements such as rotor runout.
The rotating disc that the pads squeeze to slow the wheel.
A classification of brake fluid type. The correct type must be taken from the manufacturer's specification.
The rotating housing inside which brake shoes press outward.
An electronic function that adjusts brake force between axles or wheels.
The resistance between two surfaces in contact that slows movement.
The lining on pads and shoes that creates friction against the rotor or drum.
A hard, shiny surface on friction material that reduces braking and can cause noise.
Small parts such as springs, clips, pins and shims that locate and support the brake parts.
The pressure in the brake fluid that moves the pistons at each wheel.
Able to absorb moisture from the air, as most brake fluids do.
A rated support stand used to hold a raised vehicle safely.
The friction material bonded or riveted to a brake shoe.
The component that converts pedal force into hydraulic pressure.
A precision tool used to measure thickness, such as rotor thickness.
The smallest allowed thickness of a pad, shoe lining or rotor, specified by the manufacturer.
The mechanical or electric brake that holds the vehicle when parked.
The distance the brake pedal moves between rest and full application.
A valve that limits pressure to the rear brakes to help prevent early rear lock-up.
The distance travelled while the driver notices a hazard and begins to brake.
The container on the master cylinder that stores brake fluid.
A spring that pulls the brake shoes back from the drum when the pedal is released.
The side-to-side wobble of a rotor or drum surface as it rotates.
Grooves cut into a rotor or drum surface, often by debris or worn-through friction material.
The manufacturer's document that gives specifications, procedures and torque values for a vehicle.
A pin that lets a floating caliper move so that it can apply the pads evenly.
A pedal that feels soft and elastic, often caused by air or moisture in the fluid.
Reaction distance plus braking distance.
Differences in rotor thickness around the disc that can cause pedal pulsation.
The twisting force applied to a fastener, measured in N·m or lb-ft.
A tool used to tighten fasteners to a specified torque.
A booster that uses engine vacuum acting on a diaphragm to assist the driver.
A measuring tool for lengths, diameters and depths.
A rotor with two faces and cooling vanes between them.
A tab or sensor on a pad that signals that the friction material is thin.
The hydraulic cylinder in a drum brake that pushes the shoes outward.
A sensor that measures wheel rotation speed for the ABS and stability systems.
